text: Soapy moved restlessly. <break time="0.8s" /> On his bench in Madison Square. <break time="0.8s" /> For winter was coming to New York. <break time="0.8s" /> A dead leaf fell into his lap. <break time="0.8s" /> And Soapy knew. <break time="0.8s" /> It was the card of Jack Frost. <break time="0.8s" /> Jack Frost was kind to the people. <break time="0.8s" /> Who lived in the park. <break time="0.8s" /> For he always sent a warning. <break time="0.8s" /> Before his yearly visit. <break time="0.8s" /> Soapy knew that the time had come. <break time="0.8s" /> For him to make his plans. <break time="0.8s" /> For the hard winter. <break time="0.8s" /> Soapy did not dream of a trip. <break time="0.8s" /> To the warm Mediterranean Sea. <break time="0.8s" /> Or the sunny southern skies. <break time="0.8s" /> All he wanted was three months. <break time="0.8s" /> On the Island. <break time="0.8s" /> Where he would have food. <break time="0.8s" /> A bed, and good company. <break time="0.8s" /> If he were in prison. <break time="0.8s" /> For the winter. <break time="0.8s" /> He would not have to fear. <break time="0.8s" /> The cold wind or the police. <break time="0.8s" /> Many kind groups in the city. <break time="0.8s" /> Gave beds and food to the poor. <break time="0.8s" /> But Soapy did not want their charity. <break time="0.8s" /> In return for a bed. <break time="0.8s" /> They asked many questions. <break time="0.8s" /> About his private life. <break time="0.8s" /> Which hurt his pride. <break time="0.8s" /> Soapy decided. <break time="0.8s" /> That the law was kinder than charity. <break time="0.8s" /> So he would let the law. <break time="0.8s" /> Take care of him.
